title: Astronauts and rockets
examples: What do astronauts wear when they go to space?
How does a rocket get off the ground?
Why do things float in space?

explain.say: Today you will learn about astronauts and rockets.
Now look. These are the stages of a rocket in 3D. Can you see the escape tower and the crew capsule? Tap any part to hear about it.
Astronauts wear special suits in space.
Gravity still pulls on astronauts in space. They float because they keep falling around the Earth.
At blast off, the rocket engines push hard. The rocket shoots up fast.
Things float in the space station too, like pens and water drops. It feels like there is no gravity.

draw.text: Floating: it feels like no gravity

explain.say: Astronauts practise in a big swimming pool. In the water, they feel light, a bit like in space.

faq.q: Why do astronauts float in space?
faq.a: They are falling around the Earth all the time, together with their space station. So they feel as if they weigh nothing.
asks: Why don't they fall down in space?

faq.q: What is the main job of a space suit?
faq.a: A space suit gives the astronaut air to breathe. It keeps them warm and safe.
asks: Why do astronauts need big suits?
What does the suit do for them?

faq.q: How does a rocket actually blast off?
faq.a: A rocket blasts off by burning fuel very fast to create a huge push called thrust. This push sends the rocket upward into space.
asks: What makes a rocket go fast?
How does it leave the ground?
What is thrust in a rocket?

faq.q: Is floating the same as zero gravity?
faq.a: Astronauts call it weightlessness. Gravity is still there, but they float because they keep falling around the Earth.
asks: What is the difference between floating and zero gravity?
Is low gravity the same as no gravity?

faq.q: What is the difference between a rocket and a spacecraft?
faq.a: A rocket is the vehicle that provides the power to blast off. The spacecraft is the whole vehicle that takes astronauts to their destination.
asks: Is the rocket the whole thing?

facts: Space suits provide breathable air for astronauts.
Rockets create upward motion using powerful thrust.
Astronauts float because they keep falling around the Earth with their spacecraft.
Astronauts must be trained for long missions.

quiz.say: What does a space suit give an astronaut?
quiz.why: Space has no air to breathe. The suit gives the astronaut air.

wrong.0: A space suit has no wings, and it keeps the astronaut safe.
wrong.2: Astronauts eat inside the space station, from food pouches.

quiz.say: What is the big push from a rocket's engines called?
quiz.why: Thrust is the push from the engines. It lifts the rocket up.

wrong.2: Weight is how hard gravity pulls the rocket down.

quiz.say: Why do astronauts float in the space station?

options.show: the station is full of water
options.say: the station is full of water

options.show: they keep falling around the Earth
options.say: they keep falling around the Earth

quiz.why: The astronauts and the station keep falling around the Earth together. So they float.

wrong.0: There is no wind inside the station.
wrong.1: The station is full of air, and astronauts float in it.
